east_texas.headline: Warm again today, then a cold front Sunday and a chilly Thanksgiving week.
east_texas.summary: Fog and low clouds hung around Tyler early, and by late morning backyard stations across the area read in the low to mid 70s. Partly sunny and warm this afternoon, with a high in the mid 70s. Sunday's front brings only a slight shower chance, then cooler air, and NWS says many areas could reach freezing by Thanksgiving morning.
east_texas.rain_note: Rain chance near 0% today, about 10% late tonight into Sunday morning

days.text: Cold front. A slight chance of an early shower, then sunny. West wind gusts near 25 mph, turning north at night.
Mostly sunny and cool. A reinforcing front arrives late.
Sunny. NWS says any rain with the midweek front would be light and brief, and confidence is low.
Sunny and dry for now. A freeze is possible in many areas early Thursday and again Friday morning.

facts.p: SPC's marginal risk Sunday stays in South Texas
No outages listed in Smith or nearby counties
NWS forecasts about 33 Wed night; freezing temps likely in many areas

panels.title: Turning colder, with a freeze possible
paras: NWS Shreveport says temperatures return to normal Monday, then a second front Tuesday night brings colder air through the holiday. It expects freezing temperatures in many areas on Thanksgiving morning and again on Black Friday. Any rain with that front looks light and brief, and Thanksgiving Day looks dry for now.

The Climate Prediction Center favors below-normal temperatures from eastern and southern Texas to the Gulf Coast for Nov 26–30, with wetter than normal odds near the Gulf. For Nov 28 – Dec 4 it leans near normal for temperature and wetter than normal for southern and eastern Texas.

panels.title: A strong El Niño is in charge
paras: The Climate Prediction Center says El Niño is strong to very strong and still strengthening, near +2.5°C in the key Pacific region. That usually means an active southern storm track and more cool, cloudy, wet days in East Texas.
It does not bring Arctic air on its own. Ice or snow still needs cold air from Canada.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, KLTV closings, PowerOutage.us, Weather Underground.

chips.text: Coldest night of the season tonight

nm.headline: A quick burst of mountain snow today, then the coldest night of the season.
nm.summary: A Pacific cold front is crossing the mountains, with snow showers into the afternoon. Most areas get under 2 inches, and the highest southwest-facing slopes of the Sangres could see up to 4 or 5 inches. By mid-morning, backyard stations in the mountain towns read mostly in the mid 30s to low 40s and falling. Tonight clears and turns very cold, with single digits in high valleys like Angel Fire and Red River.

days.text: Sunny and chilly after a very cold start. High clouds move in later. Light winds.
Another quick system brings snow showers Monday afternoon into Monday night. A couple of inches possible in the northern mountains; most of the snow stays in Colorado.
Sunny and cold. Teens at night in the high valleys.
Mostly sunny and near normal for Thanksgiving.
Another fast system late in the week. Models lean toward a mostly dry front, with light mountain snow possible.

nm.snow_note: Readings are from the start of today, before this morning's snow. Lower stations have been slowly melting; the highest station is holding steady.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu is open with 1 of 6 lifts and 1 trail. Its 12 in. base includes man-made snow. OpenSnow expects light snow today and Monday, several dry days over Thanksgiving, and a possible storm cycle around Nov 30 to Dec 2. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Quick snow today, coldest night tonight
paras: NWS Albuquerque says today's front brings a short burst of snow to the Jemez, Sangre de Cristo and Sandia/Manzano mountains, generally under 2 inches. Southwest-facing Sangre slopes above 10,000 ft could pick up as much as 5 inches.

Skies clear tonight and winds ease, so cold air settles into the valleys. NWS forecasts about 4 to 11 degrees at Angel Fire and near 11 at Red River, the coldest of the season so far. Protect outdoor pipes and pets.

panels.title: Mountain roads open, watch for slick spots
paras: As of late morning, NMRoads lists no weather problems on NM-518, US-64, NM-434, NM-38, NM-75, NM-150, NM-68, US-285/84 or NM-475. Expect road work on NM-434 south of Black Lake (MM 21–24).
Snow showers this afternoon can make passes and shaded canyons slick quickly, and tonight's cold will refreeze anything wet. Monday night's system may do the same.
NWS expects no critical fire weather for the next seven days.

panels.title: Dry around Thanksgiving, then maybe more active
paras: NWS Albuquerque expects a mostly dry week after Monday, with temperatures near to slightly below normal. Longer-range guidance points toward wetter and colder weather in early December, and OpenSnow is watching Nov 30 to Dec 2.
El Niño is strong and still strengthening. It usually sends more storms across the southern Rockies, which improves the odds for a snowier season here, though it does not guarantee one.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, Sipapu snow report, OnTheSnow projected openings, OpenSnow, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Weather Underground.
